description: The 3-D Building Model is a citywide three-dimensional building massing model of New York City, published on NYC Open Data by the Office of Technology and Innovation (formerly DoITT GIS) as one of its digital tools. It gives the volumes of the city's buildings for use in GIS, CAD and urban modelling software. Coverage: New York City, all five boroughs as a single citywide model; the catalogue entry was made public on 18 April 2016 and is marked as historical data with no automated updates, and the three downloadable archives on the city's media server were last modified on 1 December 2022. Format and access: three zipped downloads linked from the NYC Open Data page (tnru-abg2): CityGML (about 916 MB), Esri Multipatch (about 257 MB) and MicroStation DGN (about 762 MB), with file names beginning DA_WISE; free and without registration. Licence: no licence is set on the NYC Open Data entry; the portal's general terms of use were not read. Caveats: the data page gives no level of detail, capture date or attribute list; the older Department of City Planning download page now refuses the cloud and redirects, so any documentation there was not read; the model is a massing model and does not describe building use or construction. Simulation uses: building geometry for urban flood, wind and heat exposure analysis, line-of-sight and telecom coverage studies, and city digital twins. Related records: building footprints with heights (data-nyc-building-footprints) and tax-lot land use (data-nyc-pluto-mappluto) describe the same building stock.
